modules.doc:
## Informal definitions and lemmas

This file contains the necessary structures that must be imported into a file for it to contain
informal definitions and lemmas.

Everything else about informal definitions and lemmas are in the `Informal.Post` module.

sections.text:
## Syntax

Using macros for syntax rewriting works better with the language server compared to
`Lake.DSL.LeanLibDecl`. Hovering over any definition of `informal_definition` or `informal_lemma`
gives a proper type hint like any proper definition using `def` whereas definitions of `lake_lib`
and `lake_exe` don't show docstrings and infer the type `Lean.Name`.

declarations.name: InformalDefinition
declarations.doc: The structure representing an informal definition.
declarations.statement:
structure InformalDefinition where
  /-- The names of top-level commands we expect this definition to depend on. -/
  deps : List Lean.Name
  /-- The tag of the informal definition. This should be unique amongst informal results
    and todo items. -/
  tag : String

structure InformalLemma where
  /-- The names of top-level commands we expect this lemma to depend on. -/
  deps : List Lean.Name
  /-- The tag of the informal lemma. This should be unique amongst informal results
    and todo items. -/
  tag : String

declarations.name: «semiformal_result»
declarations.doc:
A semiformal result is either a
- definition in which the type is given but not the definition.
- proof in which the proposition is given but not the proof.
Semiformal results cannot be used in further code. They are essentially
forgot about after made.

With minor modification they act in a similar way to `proof_wanted`, however
they appear in Physlib's TODO list and must be tagged accordingly.
They must also always have a doc-string.

modules.title: Physlib exemptions for the `defsWithUnderscore` linter
modules.doc:
Mathlib's `defsWithUnderscore` environment linter reports every definition whose name contains
an underscore. Four families of Physlib declaration trip it even though the offending name is
either generated by Lean or belongs to a declaration that is not user-facing:

* `informal_definition` and `informal_lemma` elaborate to `def`s of type `InformalDefinition`
  and `InformalLemma`. They stand in for results that are not yet formalised, and they carry the
  snake_case name of the statement rather than of a definition.
* `syntax`, `notation` and `macro` declarations, together with the parenthesizer and formatter
  that Lean generates beside them. Mathlib exempts the names Lean invents for these, but Physlib
  names many of them explicitly.
* Anonymous instances whose generated name carries the suffix Lean appends to keep it unique
  across projects, `_physlib` for a declaration in `Physlib` and so on. Mathlib exempts its own
  `_mathlib` suffix in the same way.
* Anonymous instances that Lean disambiguates with a trailing number. Mathlib exempts `_1` and
  `_2` but not higher numbers such as `_3` and `_4`.

`withDefsWithUnderscoreExemptions` wraps the linter so that these pass; every other declaration
is reported as before.

declarations.name: Physlib.parserDeclTypes
declarations.doc:
The types of the declarations that `syntax`, `notation` and `macro` commands produce, along
with the pretty-printer declarations generated beside them. These hold parser data rather than
a mathematical definition, so their names are exempt from the naming convention.

declarations.name: Physlib.projectSuffix
declarations.doc:
The suffix Lean appends to the generated name of an anonymous instance to keep it unique
across projects, for example `_physlib` for a declaration of the `Physlib` project. This
mirrors `Lean.Elab.Command.NameGen.mkBaseNameWithSuffix`.
declarations.statement: def projectSuffix (env : Environment) (declName : Name) : Option String

declarations.name: Physlib.hasNumericSuffix
declarations.doc:
Whether the final component of `declName` ends in an underscore followed by a number, the
suffix Lean adds when the name it generated for an anonymous instance is already taken.

declarations.name: Physlib.defsWithUnderscoreExempt
declarations.doc: Whether the `defsWithUnderscore` linter should pass over `declName`.

declarations.name: Physlib.withDefsWithUnderscoreExemptions
declarations.doc:
`withDefsWithUnderscoreExemptions linter` behaves like `linter` except that it passes over
the declarations selected by `defsWithUnderscoreExempt`.

modules.title: The `pseudo` attribute
modules.doc:
The attribute marking declarations which depend on the `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom.

## i. Overview

This module defines the attribute `pseudo`, marking declarations that depend on the
`Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom, and the environment extension `pseudoExtension` recording them.
The check that the attribute is correctly applied is `Physlib.pseudoTest` in
`Physlib.Meta.Pseudo`.

## ii. Key results

- `pseudoExtension` : The environment extension recording the declarations attributed `pseudo`.
- `Pseudo_attr` : The `pseudo` attribute.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The `pseudo` environment extension
- B. The `pseudo` attribute

## iv. References

* None.

modules.doc:
## Underlying structure for notes

This file contains the necessary structures that must be imported into a file
for it to be turned into a Lean note.

It allows for the
- `note ...` command to be used to add notes to a Lean file
- `note_attr` attribute to be used to display formally verified commands within a note.
- `note_attr_informal` attribute to be used to display informal commands within a note.

Other results relating to notes are in other files.

modules.title: Meta results regarding the `pseudo` attribution
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The purpose of this module is to collect all results which depend on the `Lean.ofReduceBool`
axiom, and check that they are exactly the results attributed `pseudo`.

## ii. Key results

- `pseudoTest` : A test, over given libraries, that the results attributed `pseudo` are exactly
  those depending on the `Lean.ofReduceBool` axiom.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Collecting results depending on `Lean.ofReduceBool`
  - A.1. The state information to be collected
  - A.2. The monad for collecting names
  - A.3. The collection function
  - A.4. Given an array updating the state with all names depending on axioms
  - A.5. Given an array getting all names depending on axioms
  - A.6. Getting all names depending on axioms from all user defined constants
- B. Collecting all names attributed `pseudo`
- C. Testing that the `pseudo` attribution is correctly applied

## iv. References

* Adapted from `Lean.Util.CollectAxioms`, copyright (c) 2020 Microsoft
  Corporation, authored by Leonardo de Moura.

This module contains global TODO items, which are not specific to any particular module,
